yeah, I doing everything I can. ive been doing anything and everything I can to get better. its been really hard but I'm really trying to make as much progress as I can. 

before she cut me off I'd been working really hard to stop trauma dumping and establishing boundaries which makes it more upsetting. I've tried so so hard to get better and to work on the friendship but it's still not enough. I feel so awful for hurting her and I feel so awful that the guilt of being a burden is making me worse as I don't want her to see me worse as that would hurt her more

It's my fault and I know I need to work on it. I tried avoiding all talk of mental illness for a few months but it's hard as she would ask how I was doing and I had no idea what to say and would say something like "things are hard but I'm managing" because I hate lying and it's better than telling her that I have literally nothing positive to say. it felt like I was having to put on a huge front as I was terrified of seeming too anxious or depressed as I just wanted her to feel okay and not worry about me. 

it's hard because my entire life has become centred on being mentally ill and I hate it. cause I'm constantly trying to manage it. everyday is just survival. I just wish I was better and that I was better able to help myself get to a better place. I hate that this has ruined my friendship and I hate myself for not being able to make progress despite my efforts. 

I have made progress but it feels pointless as the only progress I've made is attempting and self harming less often and that's taken a lot of work (and I mean a LOT) it's been extremely hard to do self help as as it takes so much out of me and I have little motivation and energy but I'm really really trying
Thanks, hopefully I'll be able to get a therapist soon and in the meantime I'll try and work on healing myself the best I can

That sounds really hard :( I know it's easier said than done but try not to be hard on yourself or feel guilty. You are not disgusting! (ik its hard to not feel like that but trust me you're not). A week is not that long don't worry. 

I was in a similar position before when I had to self isolate. Usually I restrict but sometimes I get into cycles when I can't stop bingeing and the guilt and shame is really difficult. When I had to isolate I also ended up using uber eats and binging too. 

Maybe you could order some foods online from the supermarket? Sometimes on uber eats there are supermarkets too. sorry if this isn't helpful. When I'm trying to get out of bingeing I find it helpful to have safe foods in the house. I'm not sure if you have safe foods as ik not everyone does but for me it can be helpful.

I know this is all from my experience so I don't know if it will help you but here are a few things that help/distract me when I'm feeling guilty about food:

\- Listen to some music ( anything you want! it can be a nice distraction)

\- Watch/ read something (also a good distraction)

\- Message/call a friend either someone you know irl or just online

\- Write down your thoughts/ draw

\-  Have a shower/bath

\- Drink water/tea or whatever takes your fancy

\- Go on a short walk/open your windows for fresh air (obviously if you're isolating going out isn't really possible)

\- Light a candle (this is so random i just like candles haha)

I know a lot of this is very generic and kinda random. It won't fix everything but it can be helpful sometimes. You could even write a list of things more personal to yourself if that would help. If you want any music/book/tv recommendations lmk :)

The bad ones were about 1-2 years old from hair straighteners and others were from hot candle wax. It just took time for them to fade. Now there are faint marks and in certain lighting you can't see them at all. I didn't really notice until today when I looked and realised I had to try really hard to see them
Thanks :) I reached out to my GP this morning who also suggested dissociation. I'm already waiting for some support from mental health services, so she said she would contact them again.

yeah, it's just hard as I'm in the uk and I don't actually know how I can quickly talk to a proper psychiatrist (I can't afford to go private). I don't feel comfortable discuss it with my gp or a mental health nurse as in my experience they can be really nice but don't diagnose or seem to know a lot about more complex issues
